name: BSc Genetics
title: BSc Genetics
intro: The genetics roadmap: admission, molecular and classical genetics papers, lab techniques and research careers.

phases.title: Class 11–12 subjects
phases.summary: Science with Biology and Chemistry; Maths is helpful for statistics.
points: Most universities need Class 12 PCB with a minimum percentage.
Strengthen Biology, Chemistry and basic statistics.
Read about genomics, personalised medicine and ethics.
Look for universities with molecular biology labs.

phases.title: Entrance exams and admission
phases.summary: CUET-UG for many universities, merit or entrance for others.
points: Take CUET-UG with the science domain subjects.
Apply through the university counselling portal.
Private universities may run their own tests.
Prefer colleges with active research labs.

phases.title: Year 1: foundation papers
phases.summary: Core science papers and lab skills.
points: Core papers: Cell Biology, Biochemistry, Basic Genetics and Chemistry.
Under NEP you also take language, environment and skill-enhancement courses.
Learn to maintain a lab notebook, follow safety rules and write practical reports.
Start reading beyond the syllabus and attend department seminars.

phases.title: Year 2–3: advanced and applied papers
phases.summary: Deeper papers, electives and a project.
points: Year 2: Molecular Biology, Microbiology, Population and Evolutionary Genetics, and Biostatistics.
Year 3: Genetic Engineering, Human Genetics, Bioinformatics, Genomics and Proteomics, and a research project.
Complete a project or dissertation under a faculty guide.
Many universities offer a fourth Honours year with research.

phases.title: Lab skills, internships and training
points: Learn: PCR, gel electrophoresis, DNA extraction, microscopy, bioinformatics tools and basic Python or R.
Do summer internships or short research projects in labs, companies and government institutions.
Take certificate courses on SWAYAM, NPTEL or industry bodies.
Keep a record of your projects, certificates and skills.

phases.title: After BSc: MSc, exams and careers
phases.summary: Master’s degree, NET/JRF, government jobs or industry.
points: Further study and careers: MSc Genetics/Biotechnology, research assistant roles, genetic counselling programmes, diagnostics and biotech companies.
Exams: CUET-PG, CSIR-UGC NET, GAT-B/BET, ICMR JRF and university PhD entrances.
Research route: MSc, then CSIR-UGC NET (JRF) or GATE and a PhD.
Government exams such as SSC and state PSCs are open to science graduates.
facts: CUET-PG, CSIR-UGC NET, GAT-B/BET, ICMR JRF and university PhD entrances
